items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a sharp, modern tech-news YouTube Shorts channel. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident explainer: brisk and clear, slightly wry, never hype-y. Lean on the numbers. Take a short pause before 'Here's the catch', before each punchline, and before the final sign-off.
lines: You can now carry a petaflop in your backpack. In two thousand eight, it filled a room... and cost over a hundred million dollars. So what changed?
Rewind to two thousand eight. IBM's Roadrunner became the first computer to break a petaflop.
Nearly three hundred racks. Two point three five megawatts of power.
Now Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra claims... up to one petaflop.
So did a supercomputer just shrink into a backpack?
Roadrunner counted in big, precise, sixty-four-bit numbers.
Nvidia's R T X Spark chip hits its petaflop with tiny four-bit numbers... plus a shortcut called sparsity.
Most laptops give the graphics chip its own small memory.
This one shares a single pool. Up to one hundred and twenty-eight gigabytes.
Not all of it goes to graphics. In one test, the G P U could reach about one hundred and ten.
Enough to fit an A I model with a hundred and twenty billion parameters.
On your lap. No cloud. No server room.
The bill? From two thousand five hundred and ninety-nine dollars. The one-twenty-eight-gig version? Five thousand, eight hundred and ninety-nine.
So no, it's not a two-thousand-eight supercomputer. It's an A I lab... in a backpack.
Roadrunner drew two point three five megawatts. This one charges from a hundred-and-forty-watt brick.
This is Tech Minister. Follow for tech, minus the hype.
